title: Disconnect the shop forgets the gym's owner key in this browser only; the key keeps working on the server
what: In Settings, a gym that turned the shop on but is not online yet can press Disconnect the shop. The browser forgets the gym's owner key, but nothing tells the server, so the key stays live. Anyone who copied it earlier (a shared desk computer, an old browser) keeps full owner powers: member messages, the web page, payments to MettleUp. The button even says it needs the internet, yet it sends nothing.
expected: Disconnecting retires the key on the server too (the server already has a way to retire the old owner key), so a forgotten key cannot be used again.
fix_line: On Disconnect, ask the server to retire the key before forgetting it, and say so if it fails

items.reason: The screens reach the server only through database functions. About 30 owner_* functions: member messages, trainer questions, trainer members, PT schedule/booking/cancel/profile, Plus lock, workout of the day, gym page and photo slot, gym timings, owner_gym, owner_offers, owner_send_message, owner_billing/receipt, owner_pay_mettleup/report. All are open to anon and check the gym key themselves. Owner-only: photo slot, page save, Plus lock save, send message, billing, receipt, MettleUp pay and report (a front-desk key gets OWNER_ONLY). Desk allowed by design: reply to member messages except complaints, book PT, cancel a future PT session, set the workout of the day (staff may write workouts). A MettleUp payment report stays pending until HQ confirms it by hand.

No per-gym row rules: every table the area touches has row security on, no policy and all app rights taken away, so apps cannot read them directly; the gym check lives in the key functions. The only policies are the photo bucket's upload and read rules. Other-gym tests: talk threads and messages 0069 tests 3other and 4othergym; trainer questions 0053 3othergym and 4othergym; trainers and trainer members 0050 3othergym, 4crossgym, 6othergym; PT bookings and trainer profiles 0065 1other, 3othergym and test 4; Plus lock 0070 3other; workout of the day 0051 6a-6e; gym page 0080 test 8 and 0090 test 3; photo slots and bucket 0082 3othergym and 4borrow; timings 0036 test 5; MettleUp payments 0060 test 10; receipts 0063 7b; group messages 0025 test 12 (another gym's member dropped). Thin spots, not missing: no test of another gym cancelling a PT booking or saving a trainer profile, but both functions filter by the caller's gym.
Rule applied: every table this area touches has at least one test where another gym's key is refused or sees nothing; no new finding.
Rule applied: no live cross-gym attempt was run; only code, tests and the catalog were read.
No key pattern hit in these screens. MettleUp's own UPI and bank details are not in the code: the screen gets them from the server, owner key only.
The screens hold no AI or paid-service key; the page's visitor chat and WhatsApp sends go through the server, and the only key used is the gym's own sign-in key.
Sign-in, PIN and brute force live in the auth area (existing findings: sign-in never runs out). Here, Disconnect the shop forgets the owner key only in the browser and leaves it live on the server.

No raw HTML or eval in these screens; React escapes typed text; WhatsApp links encode the message. The server limits every box: messages 1-1000 letters, the page's About 500 with no web addresses, map links only Google Maps addresses, photo links only our own, video links only YouTube, payment reference 6-30 letters and digits; all passed as parameters. CSV exports guard cells starting with = + - @.

Two uploads. Web page photos: owner-only slot with a random 32-character name that lives 15 minutes, at most 12 open and 60 a day; private bucket, 1 MB, WebP only; another gym's folder refused; a photo is readable only while it is on a live page. Trainer photo: kept as text, checked as a JPEG of at most about 100 KB, owner or that trainer only. Not checked: the bucket trusts the declared file type, so whether the public photo address serves a non-image safely belongs to the server area.

The gym page address is public by design (a name the owner picks); photo addresses carry a random 32-character id; a MettleUp receipt number opens only for that gym's owner; the member receipt's pay link is a UPI link built in the browser, no server address. Join-code guessing belongs to the join-link areas.

These screens import only react, react-dom and the shared theme; no alert names either. Vite and Vitest alerts are build and test tools; the xlsx alerts are for Excel import, outside this area (exports here are plain CSV).
